newsItems.headline: Buffett says Trump's pick of Kevin Warsh for Fed chair was 'good choice'
US Russia sanctions bill eases threat of tariffs on China and India - Reuters
Trump says he thinks Iran and Hezbollah will be added to Russia sanctions bill - Reuters

briefing.briefing: Right now the most relevant forces for gold are a moderately weak US dollar (the DXY — an index measuring dollar strength against other currencies — sits at 100.74, which is relatively soft), a geopolitical risk index that remains elevated at 173.6 (meaning global tensions are still high, which historically supports gold as a safe-haven), and steady inflows into gold ETFs [funds that hold physical gold] for three consecutive weeks, which shows real-money buyers are still active. On recent news, the most notable headline from about 3 hours ago is Warren Buffett publicly endorsing Kevin Warsh as Trump's pick for Fed Chair — Warsh is considered a hawkish candidate [meaning he favours higher interest rates], which could eventually be dollar-positive and gold-negative if confirmed; however, markets haven't dramatically repriced yet, so this is a watch item rather than a clear trigger. A Reuters report from roughly 20 hours ago noted a Russia sanctions bill that eases tariff threats on China and India — this slightly reduces global trade tension, which can take a little safe-haven demand away from gold. The directional bias leans mildly BULLISH: the dollar is soft, geopolitical risk is high, and ETF flows remain supportive, but the Warsh news introduces uncertainty. Confidence is 5/10 — this would shift lower if dollar strength picks up on Warsh speculation, or shift higher if geopolitical news escalates. There are NO scheduled economic events on the calendar for today, which is actually helpful — it means price can move more freely on trend rather than news spikes. The calendar is completely empty for the rest of the week too, so there is no major data build-up caution needed right now. On key levels: the 14-day average daily range [the typical daily price swing] is about 100 points, and today has already used roughly 56.6 of those points, meaning only around 43–44 points of typical movement may remain in today's session — price is already more than halfway through its expected daily range, so chasing large moves from here carries more risk. Watch 4046 as the current pivot; a hold above it keeps the short-term structure bullish, while a break below 4020–4010 would suggest the trend is weakening. For trade integration: this is a reasonable window for cautious trend-following long [buy] setups using your 1H trend, 5M signal, and 1M entry process, but reduce your normal position size by around 30–40% given that much of today's range is already used and the Warsh news adds uncertainty. Remember: with more than half the day's expected range already consumed, the best move is to wait for a clean pullback to a key level rather than buying into extended price.
